unreleased: The event calendar module now builds on articles: an event is just a date (or a run of days, with optional times, a title and a description of up to 128 characters) belonging to exactly one article, an article can have several. The wall (/dashboard) is made of articles - the one with the nearest upcoming date, the pinned ones and the last five past ones - the calendar, archive and search follow the article's visibility (archived articles stay findable), and search also looks through the article text ignoring diacritics. GET /by-article/{id} lists an article's dates. Events no longer have their own page, slug, image, status or pinned flag, and image upload moved to the articles module. The database table is recreated: existing events are NOT carried over

Add an articles module (app/modules/articles): articles with a title, perex, sanitized HTML content, image, status (draft / published / archived), optional display window, a pinned flag and a type, plus dynamic article types with frame and background colours for the light and dark theme. Public listing, search ignoring case and diacritics over title, perex and full text (archived articles included, drafts never), detail by slug, and administrator-only management with image upload; a type in use is deleted only with a replacement type

The shared HTML sanitizer now also keeps tables, text alignment, horizontal rules, code blocks and YouTube / Vimeo video embeds; frames from any other address, and anything that could run script, are still removed on every save

A module can declare the modules it requires (`ModuleManifest.requires`); enabling one without them now logs a warning at startup, naming both, instead of failing later in some request. The warning never stops the application

Add a portfolio module (app/modules/portfolio): projects with a Czech and an English title, short description and text, a link, a status (live or in preparation), tags and a publish flag, kept in an order the administrator sets. GET /api/modules/portfolio/items and /items/{slug} serve the published ones in the visitor's language, falling back to the other language when a text is missing; administrators manage them, reorder them and publish or hide them under /manage. The migration adds the table and seeds five projects

Add the freelancer module with GET /api/modules/freelancer/provider, which gives the legal pages the provider's details from PROVIDER_* in .env (name, company ID, address, registration, email, phone, effective date) and says whether the minimum is filled in

Switch on the contact-form module for this site, with its page heading, introduction and note, the address that receives messages shown as a contact detail, and the confirmation email written in the first person

Contact-form module: GET /api/modules/kontaktni_formular/info serves a per-language page heading, introduction and note (the new `page` block of backend/modules/kontaktni_formular.json) plus public contact details - address, GitHub and LinkedIn links from CONTACT_ADDRESS / CONTACT_GITHUB_URL / CONTACT_LINKEDIN_URL in .env, and the delivery address only when `show_email` is on. Nothing is shown until it is configured
Switch on the CRM module for this site: its partner, task and invoice endpoints are mounted under /api/modules/crm and open to administrators only

Add a CRM module (app/modules/crm), for administrators only: partners with contact and company details, their tasks (status, price, dates), and invoice PDFs uploaded against a task - checked to really be PDFs and capped at 10 MB, stored privately under uploads/crm/ and served only to administrators through an authenticated download
